function.mechanism: Chain-breaking antioxidant in lipid systems; used to inhibit oxidation in fat/oil-containing foods (functional inference from regulatory use limits).
common_food_categories: processed foods where antioxidant content is regulated relative to fat/oil

adi.basis: Temporary ADI set by EFSA ANS Panel in the 2012 re-evaluation (EFSA Journal 2012;10(3):2588).

efsa.key_finding: No safety concern at currently permitted uses and use levels, but ADI exceedance possible in maximum-permitted-level scenarios.

adi.basis: WHO JECFA database entry reports ADI range 0-0.3 mg/kg bw.

concerns.summary: Recent experimental studies report developmental toxicity signals for BHT metabolites (zebrafish) and altered differentiation signatures in human embryonic stem-cell models for synthetic phenolic antioxidants including BHT transformation products.
A 2025 zebrafish study reported spinal malformations/scoliosis and reduced motility, with proposed Hedgehog-pathway inhibition mechanism after BHT exposure.
Human biomonitoring in Germany found widespread detection of a BHT metabolite and highlighted uncertainty in metabolism-based reverse dosimetry, especially for children.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA ANS Panel (2012) concluded no safety concern at currently permitted uses and use levels.
IARC classification dataset lists BHT in Group 3.

adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA reported mean exposure up to 0.31 mg/kg bw/day and high exposure up to 1.29 mg/kg bw/day in younger groups; exceedance also projected if all foods contain BHT at maximum permitted levels.

risk_assessment.rationale: BHT remains authorized by major regulators with numeric intake limits, but EFSA's temporary ADI, modeled exceedance scenarios, and recent mechanistic/developmental toxicity findings support a caveated mid-tier risk classification rather than risk-free/limited.
key_factors: EFSA temporary ADI (0.25 mg/kg bw/day) and exceedance scenarios
FDA GRAS status with concentration constraints
Recent developmental/mechanistic toxicity signals in zebrafish and hESC models
